target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Bandera County Lost Maples / Edwards Plateau documentation; Real County spring-fed fen and Roaring Springs documentation; Uvalde County wild-collection associate documentation from Frio River headwaters.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; no broad-range inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the middle-sized fruit and leaflet count. Arizona walnut usually carries 9–15 broader leaflets and fruits about 2–3.5 cm across—larger than little walnut but far smaller than typical black walnut fruit.
diagnostic_traits: nut 1.8–2.7 cm, deeply longitudinally grooved but relatively smooth between grooves
streams, rocky canyon sides, springs and mesic canyon woodland

confusers.separator: J. microcarpa has 17–25 much narrower leaflets and tiny fruit; J. nigra has 15–23 leaflets plus much larger 3.5–8 cm fruit and coarsely warty nut sculpture.

caveat: Flora of North America notes intermediates among central Texas Juglans, so atypical trees should be checked with fruit/nut characters as well as leaflet count.
